title: PRRG4 Brain-Specific Conditional Knockout Mice Display Autism Spectrum Disorder-Like Behaviors
author: Shen, Chen, et al.
materials: To prepare the PRRG4 affinity column, purified PRRG4 antigen (~ 1 mg) was covalently crosslinked to the SulfoLink™ Coupling Resin (Thermo Fisher, Massachusetts, USA) according to the manufacturer’s instruction. Rabbit sera from rabbits immunized with His-tagged mouse PRRG4 protein (aa135-226) were generated by HUABIO (Hangzhou, China). PRRG4 serum (2 ml) was added to the PRRG4 affinity column and incubated with rotation at 4℃ overnight. The bound PRRG4 antibodies were washed and eluted with 100 mM glycine, pH 2.5.

steps.title: Anesthetize and dissect mouse brains
steps.instruction: Anesthetize 3‑month‑old male mice (3 mice per group) with 1.5 % isoflurane inhalation, then dissect out the whole brain.

steps.title: Impregnate tissue with Golgi solutions
steps.instruction: Immerse the dissected brain in a 1:1 mixture of Golgi solution A and solution B at room temperature in the dark for 2 weeks; then transfer to solution C at room temperature in the dark for 3 days; finally place the tissue at –80 °C for at least 1 hour.

steps.title: Section and process tissue for staining
steps.instruction: Cut 100 µm coronal sections of cerebral cortex and hippocampus, air‑dry them naturally at room temperature in the dark, then alkalize by immersing in a mixture of solution D, solution E and ddH₂O (1:1:2) for 10 min. Dehydrate the sections with ethanol, permeate with xylene, and mount coverslips.

steps.title: Capture microscopic images
steps.instruction: Observe the stained sections under a microscope and acquire images of pyramidal neurons.

steps.title: Analyze dendritic morphology with ImageJ
steps.instruction: Use ImageJ with the Neuroanatomy‑SNT plugin to visualize neurons, trace dendrites, and measure total dendritic length per pyramidal neuron; apply the Neuroanatomy‑Sholl plugin to draw concentric circles (10 µm radial increment) centered on the soma and record intersection counts as branching metrics; count dendritic spines with ImageJ, measure dendritic length with the Segmented line plugin, and calculate spine density as spines per 10 µm of dendrite.

steps.title: Express and purify His‑PRRG4 antigen protein
steps.instruction: Induce E. coli carrying the PET‑28a vector for His‑tagged mouse PRRG4 (aa 135‑226) with IPTG (final 1 mmol L⁻¹) at 37 °C for 4 h; centrifuge at 4 °C, 4000 rpm for 10 min; resuspend pellets in denaturing lysis buffer (8 M urea, 2 mM PMSF) and lyse by sonication; mix the lysate with nickel‑column resin and incubate on a 4 °C rotary shaker overnight; wash the resin repeatedly with denaturing lysis buffer, elute with denaturing elution buffer, and renature the eluted protein by dialysis against PBS.

steps.title: Purify rabbit anti‑mouse PRRG4 antibody
steps.instruction: Crosslink ~1 mg purified PRRG4 antigen to SulfoLink™ Coupling Resin (Thermo Fisher) according to the manufacturer’s protocol to create an affinity column; add 2 ml rabbit serum (generated by HUABIO against His‑PRRG4 aa 135‑226) to the column and rotate at 4 °C overnight; wash the column and elute bound antibodies with 100 mM glycine, pH 2.5.

steps.title: Perform statistical analysis
steps.instruction: Analyze data using GraphPad Prism 9.0; test variance homogeneity first, then apply an unpaired t‑test for two‑group comparisons or ANOVA for three or more groups; if variances are homogeneous use Tukey’s post‑hoc test, if heterogeneous use Tamhane’s T2; consider P < 0.05 as significant.
